key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against environmental degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, durable hybrid photovoltaics on untextured silicon by combining complementary optical, electrical, and barrier functions.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Evaluate efficiency retention after 75 days of ambient exposure.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, compared with approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75-day ambient aging; longer-term durability and manufacturing-scale graphene barrier integrity remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
